about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Lemony Roast Chicken Leftovers Soup with Egg Noodles and Parsley
recipes.summary: A comforting soup that turns the last of the roast chicken into a quick weeknight meal.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrots and celery over medium heat for 6 minutes until softened, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Pour in the stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes until the carrots are tender.
Add the noodles and chicken and simmer for 5 minutes until the noodles are cooked and the chicken is steaming hot at 75°C, then stir in the lemon juice, parsley and salt.
notes: Food safety: use roast chicken within 3 days of cooking, keep it chilled, and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C all the way through.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Leftover Roast Chicken Congee
recipes.summary: A silky rice porridge made with leftover roast chicken, ginger and spring onion.
steps: Put the rice, stock and ginger in a large pot and bring to a gentle boil, stirring until the rice begins to bubble.
Reduce to a low simmer and cook for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice breaks down into a thick, creamy porridge.
Stir in the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then season with the soy sauce, sesame oil and pepper and top with the spring onions.
notes: Food safety: cool leftover congee and refrigerate within 1 hour, because cooked rice can grow harmful bacteria, and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Add water if it thickens too much on standing.

recipes.title: Leftover Roast Lamb Scotch Broth
recipes.summary: A hearty barley broth that makes the most of Sunday's roast lamb and any bone.
steps: Soften the onion, carrots, swede and leeks in the oil in a large pot over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add the barley, stock and bay leaves and simmer for 40 minutes until the barley and vegetables are tender.
Stir in the lamb and cook for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then season and finish with the parsley.
notes: Food safety: use roast lamb within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
The soup thickens overnight; thin with a little water.

recipes.title: Next Day Roast Beef Pearl Barley Soup with Carrot and Turnip
recipes.summary: A rich, beefy soup with barley, built on leftover roast beef and its pan juices.
steps: Cook the onion, carrots, turnip and celery in the oil in a large pot for 8 minutes until softened, then add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the barley, stock and thyme and simmer for 40 minutes until the barley is tender.
Stir in the beef and Worcestershire sauce and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then season with salt.
notes: Food safety: eat roast beef within 3 days of cooking and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Freezes for 2 months.

recipes.title: Next Day Roast Pork Shreds in Caraway Cabbage Broth
recipes.summary: A warming Eastern European soup with shredded pork, cabbage and caraway.
steps: Cook the onion and carrots in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft, then add the caraway for 1 minute.
Add the cabbage, stock and potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the pork and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then add the vinegar, salt and dill.
notes: Food safety: use roast pork within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Serve with rye bread.

recipes.title: Leftover Chicken and Rice Soup with Carrot and Celery
recipes.summary: Shredded leftover roast chicken simmered with rice, carrot and celery in a savoury broth.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the stock, bay leaves, rice, carrots and celery and simmer for 18 minutes until the rice and vegetables are tender.
Add the chicken and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then season with salt and parsley.
notes: Food safety: use roast chicken within 3 days of cooking, and refrigerate the soup within 1 hour of cooking because it contains cooked rice.
Use the carcass to make stock separately if you like.

recipes.title: Leftover Roast Vegetable Soup
recipes.summary: Blitz the tray of roasted vegetables from yesterday into a velvety soup.

items: 600g leftover roasted vegetables (pumpkin, carrot, potato, onion)

steps: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the garlic and spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the vegetables and stock and simmer for 12 minutes until completely heated through and soft.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and salt, and top with parsley.
notes: Add a squeeze of lemon for brightness.
Use leftovers within 3 days; freezes for 2 months.

recipes.title: Roast Chicken Tortilla Soup
recipes.summary: A smoky tomato and lime soup with shredded roast chicken and crisp tortilla strips.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until slightly thickened.

Add the chicken and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, while baking the tortilla strips at 200°C for 8 minutes until crisp, then serve topped with strips, avocado, lime juice and coriander.
notes: Food safety: use roast chicken within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Add chilli if you like heat.

recipes.title: Christmas Ham Bone Soup with Split Peas and Smoked Paprika
recipes.summary: A thick, smoky split pea soup made with the leftover Christmas ham bone.

items: 1 leftover ham bone with some meat

steps: Soften the onion, carrots and celery in the oil in a large pot for 6 minutes, stirring in the paprika for the last minute.
Add the ham bone, water, split peas and bay leaves and simmer gently for 90 minutes until the peas have collapsed into a thick soup.
Lift out the bone, shred the meat back into the soup, season with pepper and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C.
notes: Food safety: use the ham bone within 3 days and reheat the soup until steaming hot at 75°C.
The ham is already salty, so taste before adding any salt.

recipes.title: Silky Roast Pumpkin Soup Finished with Coconut Cream and Lime Zest
recipes.summary: Leftover roasted pumpkin blitzed with coconut cream, ginger and lime for a velvety soup.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft, then add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the pumpkin and stock and simmer for 10 minutes until completely hot.
Blend until smooth, stir in the coconut cream, lime juice and salt and top with lime zest.
notes: Cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours.
Freezes for 2 months.

recipes.title: Shredded Roast Lamb Moroccan Harira with Lentils Chickpeas and Tomato
recipes.summary: A warming spiced soup of lentils, chickpeas and tomato with the last of the roast lamb.
steps: Cook the onion and celery in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, lentils, chickpeas and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the lamb and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then add the lemon juice, coriander and salt.
notes: Food safety: use roast lamb within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Roast Chicken Laksa-Style Soup
recipes.summary: A coconut curry noodle soup that revives leftover roast chicken in 20 minutes.
steps: Fry the laksa paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and stock and simmer for 8 minutes, then add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C.
Soak the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, drain into bowls and ladle over the soup, then top with sprouts, lime juice, fish sauce and coriander.
notes: Food safety: use roast chicken within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Add chilli oil for extra heat.

recipes.title: Greek Avgolemono Soup with Leftover Roast Chicken
recipes.summary: A silky Greek-style lemon soup with rice, chicken and egg-thickened broth.
steps: Simmer the stock and rice in a pot for 15 minutes until the rice is tender.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice, then slowly whisk in 1 cup of hot stock to temper them.
Return the mixture to the pot off the heat with the chicken, stirring gently for 3 minutes until hot at 75°C and slightly thickened, then season and add the dill.
notes: Food safety: keep the soup below a boil once the egg is added, and make sure the soup reaches 75°C so the egg is cooked through.
Use roast chicken within 3 days of cooking.

recipes.title: Oven Tray Baked Eggs and Sausages for a Crowd
recipes.summary: A hands-off breakfast tray of sausages, tomatoes and baked eggs for a full table.
steps: Toss the sausages, tomatoes and mushrooms with the oil on a large tray and roast at 200°C for 15 minutes until the sausages are browned.
Make 8 small wells in the vegetables and crack an egg into each.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the whites are set and the sausages reach 75°C in the centre, then season and add parsley.
notes: Food safety: cook the sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre and the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Serve with toast.

recipes.title: Baked French Toast Casserole for Eight
recipes.summary: A custardy cinnamon French toast bake that feeds a crowd from one dish.
steps: Spread the bread cubes in a buttered baking dish and drizzle with the melted butter.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt, then pour evenly over the bread and press down.
Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until puffed, golden and the custard is set in the centre.
notes: Food safety: bake until the egg custard is fully set and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Serve with fruit and maple syrup.

recipes.title: Big Pot Oat Porridge for Eight
recipes.summary: A creamy porridge cooked on the stove for a crowd, ready for any toppings.
steps: Put the oats, milk, water and salt in a large saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the honey and cinnamon and add a splash of milk if too thick.
notes: Set out bowls of fruit, nuts and seeds for toppings.
Stir regularly to prevent catching.

recipes.title: Breakfast Burrito Tray Bake
recipes.summary: Oven-baked burritos filled with eggs, beans and cheese, made in bulk for a brunch table.
steps: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the beaten eggs, cumin and salt and stir for 3 minutes until just set.
Stir in the beans, spoon the filling onto the tortillas with the cheese and roll tightly.
Bake seam-side down at 200°C for 12 minutes until golden and hot throughout.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm and bake until steaming hot, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Freeze wrapped burritos for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Brunch Frittata Squares
recipes.summary: A tray-baked frittata of spinach, capsicum and feta, cut into squares for sharing.
steps: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then wilt in the spinach for 1 minute.
Whisk the eggs, cream, salt and pepper and stir in the vegetables and feta.
Pour into a lined 20x30cm tray and bake at 180°C for 22 minutes until set and lightly golden.
notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is completely set and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Make-Ahead Egg and Bacon Muffins
recipes.summary: Savoury egg muffins with bacon and cheese that reheat in a minute.
steps: Fry the bacon in the oil for 6 minutes until crisp, then drain.
Whisk the eggs with the salt and pepper and stir in the bacon, cheese and spring onions.
Pour into a greased 12-hole muffin tray and bake at 180°C for 18 minutes until puffed and set in the centre.
notes: Food safety: bake until the eggs are fully set and refrigerate within 2 hours; reheat until steaming hot.
Freezes for 1 month.

recipes.title: Oven Baked Pancake Tray for a Crowd
recipes.summary: A single-tray pancake that puffs and browns in the oven, so nobody is flipping at the stove.
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, butter and vanilla, pour into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Pour into a lined 25x35cm tray and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden, then cut into squares.
notes: Food safety: bake until set in the centre.
Serve with berries and maple syrup.

recipes.title: Baked Shakshuka for Six
recipes.summary: A big dish of spiced tomato and capsicum sauce with baked eggs.
steps: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 12 minutes until thick.
Make 6 wells, crack in the eggs, scatter with feta and bake at 190°C for 10 minutes until the whites are set, then add parsley.
notes: Food safety: cook until the egg whites are fully set.
Serve with warm flatbread.

recipes.title: Oven Hash Browns Tray with Capsicum Onion and Sausage Crumble for Twelve
recipes.summary: A big oven-baked hash with crisp potato, capsicum, onion and browned sausage.

items: 4 pork sausages, meat squeezed from casings

steps: Toss the potatoes, capsicums, onions, oil, paprika, salt and pepper on two large trays and roast at 220°C for 20 minutes.
Add the sausage meat in small pieces and roast for 20 minutes more, stirring once, until the potatoes are crisp and the sausage is cooked through at 75°C.
Season and serve straight from the tray.
notes: Food safety: make sure the sausage is cooked until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C.
Use two trays so the potatoes crisp up.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Black Bean Oven Tray Topped with Baked Eggs and Avocado
recipes.summary: Roasted sweet potato and black beans with baked eggs, avocado and lime.
steps: Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, spices and salt on a tray and roast at 210°C for 20 minutes until tender.
Add the beans, make 6 wells, crack an egg into each and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the whites are set.
Top with avocado, lime juice and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook until the egg whites are fully set.
Add chilli sauce if you like.

recipes.title: Cheddar and Mushroom Breakfast Strata
recipes.summary: A savoury bread and egg bake with mushrooms and cheddar, ideal for brunch.
steps: Cook the mushrooms and onion in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until browned.
Layer the bread, mushrooms and half the cheese in a baking dish.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard, salt and pepper, pour over, top with the remaining cheese and bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the centre.
notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is fully set and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Assemble the night before and keep chilled.

recipes.title: Apple Cinnamon Oat Breakfast Bake for a Crowd
recipes.summary: A soft, gently sweet oat bake with apple, cinnamon and walnuts.
steps: Mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the apples with the eggs, milk and maple syrup and stir into the oats with half the walnuts.
Pour into a baking dish, scatter with the remaining walnuts and bake at 180°C for 30 minutes until golden and set.
notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is set in the centre.
Serve with yoghurt and fruit; reheats well.

recipes.title: Apple Bircher Muesli Big Bowl with Toasted Seeds for Brunch Guests
recipes.summary: A fresh, chilled apple muesli with yoghurt and toasted seeds.
steps: Toast the pumpkin and sunflower seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until golden, then cool.
Mix the oats, apple juice, apples, yoghurt, honey and cinnamon.
Cover, chill until the oats have softened, then serve topped with seeds.
notes: Soaking time is not included in the prep time.
Keeps for 3 days.
